requirements.evidence: All contract points covered: migrations match the data model (create_totem_presets_table.php:16-24, composite PK in create_totem_preset_queue_table.php:19); pairing command with random_int zero-padded code, 10 min TTL, consumed cleared, audit log, FAILURE on unknown id (OpenTotemPairing.php:21-48, TotemPairingCode.php:18-24); POST api/totem/auth 400/401/200 with entity pair, lockForUpdate transaction plus conditional update (PairTotem.php:27-79, TotemAuthController.php:23-48); JWT claims totem_id/entity_id/preset_id/queues/iat/exp/jti (PairTotem.php:69-77); middleware 401 cases and claim ∩ current join (AuthenticateTotem.php:27-55); 403/404/422 resolution order (TotemQueueController.php:104-126); priorities 0/10/20 from one enum (TicketPriority.php); issuance via IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (TotemQueueController.php:88); throttles 10/30 per minute and JSON rate_limited render (AppServiceProvider.php:39-42, bootstrap/app.php:32-36); CORS pattern for localhost/127.0.0.1 plus TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN, no credentials (config/cors.php); .env.example and phpunit.xml pinned secret/TTL; docs updated from proposal to implemented.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through Actions (PairTotem, OpenTotemPairing, reuses IssueTicket); deliberate #[Fillable] that excludes login_code* (TotemPreset.php:13); migrations have reversible down() and generator-style timestamps/stubs; CHANGELOG, docs/api/totem.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md, business-rules.md all updated. Deviations: input is checked by hand (preg_match in TotemAuthController.php:23 and TotemQueueController.php:78-81) instead of $request->validate, which the custom error codes justify but goes against the stated pattern; authorization is done in the controller/middleware (authorizeEntity/forbidden) and not through a policy or gate. The architecture.md edit also leaves one very long line.

security.evidence: JWT verification only accepts alg HS256, uses hash_equals and requires exp (TotemJwt.php:44-58); secret must be at least 32 chars (TotemJwt.php:66-68); one 401 for every pairing failure, with no oracle (PairTotem.php:34-57); single-use consumption holds under a race (conditional update, PairTotem.php:50-57); the full code is never logged (TotemAuthController.php:24,32,37-41); totem/preset/entity are re-checked on every call and scope uses the current join limited to the preset's entity (TotemPreset.php entityQueueIds, AuthenticateTotem.php:39-55); queues are resolved inside the token's entity (TotemQueueController.php:108-111); CORS is restricted by an anchored regex and credentials are off. No weaknesses found.

tests.evidence: Six Pest files: TotemAuthTest (format 400 dataset, 401 parity for unknown/expired/consumed/inactive, soft-deleted entity, throttle 429 with Retry-After, audit with no code), TotemEndpointsTest (missing/malformed/forged/expired tokens, claim/state mismatch, last_seen_at, claim∩join, foreign entity 403, 404/403/422 resolution, sequential codes through IssueTicket, invalid priorities create nothing, issuance throttle per totem, unauthenticated calls not counted), TotemCorsTest (allowed/denied origins incl. localhost.evil.example, preflight 204, outside api/*), TotemJwtTest (tamper, alg, exp, short secret), TotemModelsTest (factory, uniqueness, cascades, mass-assignment), TotemPairingTest (zero-padding, replace, unknown id, audit).

simplicity.evidence: Reuses IssueTicket and Laravel's built-in CORS/throttle middleware; the hand-rolled HS256 is small (~90 lines) and the task allows it; the priorities enum is a single source. OpenTotemPairing.php:20-47 uses a retry loop with both a pre-check and a catch, which is more complex than needed, and the pre-check `continue` never increments toward the bound.

readability.evidence: Clear names, small private helpers (resolveQueue, authorizeEntity, queueAppearance) and useful PHPDoc. Minor issues: the pairedTotem() docblock in tests/Pest.php says 'an entity with two queues' but the helper creates one; docs/architecture.md:65 has an overlong unwrapped line; request attributes ('totem_entity', 'totem_queue_ids') are untyped string keys.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models/migrations/factories, actions, command, controllers, middleware, config, routes, docs and tests. The docs/README.md and business-rules.md touches are part of the docs-sync convention. No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Entity/queue-scope authorization is hand-rolled in the controller and middleware; the conventions route authorization through policies/gates.
Input is validated with hand-written preg_match checks rather than $request->validate(); this is defensible because the contract needs custom error bodies, but it departs from the documented pattern.
The retry loop has an unbounded `continue` on the exists() pre-check (only the QueryException path is bounded) and mixes two collision strategies where one would do.
The pairedTotem() docblock says the entity has two queues, but the helper creates only one.
The new paragraph runs a sentence into one very long unwrapped line, which breaks the file's wrapping.

review.summary: The change implements the totem BFF in full: tables, models, factories, the pairing command, the code-to-JWT exchange with atomic single-use consumption, a strict HS256 middleware with intersected queue scope, the three data endpoints (issuance reuses IssueTicket), throttling with JSON 429, local-only CORS, and updated docs and config. The tests cover the happy paths and the failure, tamper and authorization paths. I'd approve with nits: authorization and validation are hand-rolled instead of using policies and $request->validate (justified by the custom error contract), plus a few small readability and simplicity issues.
